# Metadata format version 3.2 
The format version 3.2 of Argo metadata will replace version 3.1 gradually. During the transition period, all formats will be valid.

An Argo metadata file contains descriptive information about an Argo float.

For file naming conventions, see [<u>§4.1</u>](#data-access).

All variables are mandatory when not otherwise stated in the comment column of the tables.

## Global attributes
The global attributes section is used for data discovery. It complies with NetCDF Climate and Forecast (CF) Metadata Conventions (version 1.6).

- [<u>http://cfconventions.org/</u>](http://cfconventions.org/)

The following global attributes should appear in the global section (attributes in italic are optional attributes):

// global attributes:

:title = "Argo float metadata file";

:institution = "CSIRO";

:source = "Argo float";

:history = "2011-04-22T06:00:00Z creation";

:references = "[<u>http://www.argodatamgt.org/Documentation</u>](http://www.argodatamgt.org/Documentation)";

*:id = "[<u>https://doi.org/10.17882/42182</u>](https://doi.org/10.17882/42182)"*

:comment = "free text";

:user_manual_version = "3.45";

:Conventions = "Argo-3.2 CF-1.6";

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 21%" />
<col style="width: 78%" />
</colgroup>
<tbody>
<tr class="odd">
<td><strong>Global attribute name</strong></td>
<td><strong>Definition</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>title</td>
<td>A succinct description of what is in the dataset.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>institution</td>
<td>Specifies where the original data was produced.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>source</td>
<td>The method of production of the original data. If it was model-generated, source should name the model and its version, as specifically as could be useful. If it is observational, source should characterize it (e.g., "surface observation" or "radiosonde").</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>history</td>
<td>Provides an audit trail for modifications to the original data. Well-behaved generic NetCDF filters will automatically append their name and the parameters with which they were invoked to the global history attribute of an input NetCDF file. We recommend that each line begins with a timestamp indicating the date and time of day that the program was executed.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>references</td>
<td>Published or web-based references that describe the data or methods used to produce it.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>id</td>
<td><p>The Argo GDAC data DOI: <a href="https://doi.org/10.17882/42182"><u>https://doi.org/10.17882/42182</u></a></p>
<p>This attribute is <strong>optional</strong> but highly recommended</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>comment</td>
<td>Miscellaneous information about the data or methods used to produce it.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>user_manual_version</td>
<td>The version number of the user manual</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>Conventions</td>
<td>The conventions supported by this file, blank separated</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

## Dimensions and definitions 
<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 24%" />
<col style="width: 28%" />
<col style="width: 47%" />
</colgroup>
<tbody>
<tr class="odd">
<td><strong>Name</strong></td>
<td><strong>Definition</strong></td>
<td><strong>Comment</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DATE_TIME</td>
<td>DATE_TIME = 14;</td>
<td><p>This dimension is the length of an ASCII date and time value.</p>
<p>Date_time convention is : YYYYMMDDHHMISS</p>
<p>YYYY : year</p>
<p>MM : month</p>
<p>DD : day</p>
<p>HH : hour of the day</p>
<p>MI : minutes</p>
<p>SS : seconds</p>
<p>Date and time values are always in universal time coordinates (UTC).</p>
<p>Examples : 20010105172834 : January 5th 2001 17:28:34 19971217000000 : December 17th 1997 00:00:00</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td><p>STRING8192</p>
<p>STRING4096</p>
<p>STRING1024</p>
<p>STRING256</p>
<p>STRING128</p>
<p>STRING64</p>
<p>STRING32</p>
<p>STRING17</p>
<p>STRING16</p>
<p>STRING8</p>
<p>STRING4</p>
<p>STRING2</p></td>
<td><p>STRING8192 = 8192;</p>
<p>STRING4096 = 4096;</p>
<p>STRING1024 = 1024;</p>
<p>STRING256 = 256;</p>
<p>STRING128 = 128;</p>
<p>STRING64 = 64;</p>
<p>STRING32 = 32;</p>
<p>STRING17 = 17;</p>
<p>STRING16 = 16;</p>
<p>STRING8 = 8;</p>
<p>STRING4 = 4;</p>
<p>STRING2 = 2;</p></td>
<td><p>String dimensions from 2 to 8192.</p>
<p>STRING4096 and STRING8192 are optional (see <a href="#float-predeployment-calibration-information"><u>§2.4.8</u></a>)</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>N_PARAM</td>
<td>N_PARAM = &lt;int value&gt;;</td>
<td><p>Number of parameters measured or calculated for a pressure sample.</p>
<p>Examples :</p>
<p>(pressure, temperature) : N_PARAM = 2</p>
<p>(pressure, temperature, salinity) : N_PARAM = 3 (pressure, temperature, conductivity, salinity) : N_PARAM = 4</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>N_SENSOR</td>
<td>N_SENSOR = &lt;int value&gt;;</td>
<td>Number of sensors mounted on the float and used to measure the parameters.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>N_CONFIG_PARAM</td>
<td>N_CONFIG_PARAM=&lt;int value&gt;;</td>
<td>Number of configuration parameters.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>N_LAUNCH_CONFIG_PARAM</td>
<td>N_LAUNCH_CONFIG_PARAM=&lt;int value&gt;;</td>
<td>Number of pre-deployment or launch configuration parameters.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>N_MISSIONS</td>
<td>N_MISSIONS=&lt;unlimited&gt;;</td>
<td>Number of missions.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>N_POSITIONING_SYSTEM</td>
<td>N_POSITIONING_SYSTEM=&lt;int value&gt;;</td>
<td>Number of positioning systems.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>N_TRANS_SYSTEM</td>
<td>N_TRANS_SYSTEM=&lt;int value&gt;;</td>
<td>Number of transmission systems.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

## General information on the metadata file 
This section contains information about the whole file.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 19%" />
<col style="width: 46%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
</colgroup>
<tbody>
<tr class="odd">
<td><strong>Name</strong></td>
<td><strong>Definition</strong></td>
<td><strong>Comment</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DATA_TYPE</td>
<td><p>char DATA_TYPE(STRING16);</p>
<p>DATA_TYPE:long_name = "Data type";</p>
<p>DATA_TYPE:conventions = "Argo reference table 1";</p>
<p>DATA_TYPE:_FillValue = " ";</p></td>
<td><p>This field contains the type of data contained in the file.</p>
<p>The list of acceptable data types is in the reference table 1 (<a href="https://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/R01/"><u>https://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/R01/</u></a>).</p>
<p>For the metadata file, the value must be set to "Argo meta-data"</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>FORMAT_VERSION</td>
<td><p>char FORMAT_VERSION(STRING4);</p>
<p>FORMAT_VERSION:long_name = "File format version";</p>
<p>FORMAT_VERSION:_FillValue = " ";</p></td>
<td><p>File format version.</p>
<p>Example: "3.2"</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td><del>HANDBOOK_VERSION</del></td>
<td><p><del>char HANDBOOK_VERSION(STRING4);</del></p>
<p><del>HANDBOOK_VERSION:long_name = "Data handbook version";</del></p>
<p><del>HANDBOOK_VERSION:_FillValue = " ";</del></p></td>
<td><p>REMOVED in meta FORMAT_VERSION 3.2: <del>Version number of the data handbook. This field indicates that the data contained in this file are managed according to the policy described in the Argo data management handbook.</del></p>
<p><del>Example: "1.0"</del></p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>DATE_CREATION</td>
<td><p>char DATE_CREATION(DATE_TIME);</p>
<p>DATE_CREATION:long_name = "Date of file creation";</p>
<p>DATE_CREATION:conventions = "YYYYMMDDHHMISS";</p>
<p>DATE_CREATION:_FillValue = " ";</p></td>
<td><p>Date and time (UTC) of creation of this file.</p>
<p>Example: "20011229161700" (meaning December 29th 2001 16:17:00)</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DATE_UPDATE</td>
<td><p>char DATE_UPDATE(DATE_TIME);</p>
<p>DATE_UPDATE:long_name = "Date of update of this file";</p>
<p>DATE_UPDATE:conventions = "YYYYMMDDHHMISS";</p>
<p>DATE_UPDATE:_FillValue = " ";</p></td>
<td><p>Date and time (UTC) of update of this file.</p>
<p>Example: "20011230090500" (meaning December 30th 2001 09:05:00)</p></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

## Float characteristics 
This section contains the main characteristics of the float.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 28%" />
<col style="width: 40%" />
<col style="width: 31%" />
</colgroup>
<tbody>
<tr class="odd">
<td><strong>Name</strong></td>
<td><strong>Definition</strong></td>
<td><strong>Comment</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>PLATFORM_NUMBER</td>
<td><p>char PLATFORM_NUMBER(STRING8);</p>
<p>PLATFORM_NUMBER:long_name = "Float unique identifier";</p>
<p>PLATFORM_NUMBER:conventions = "WMO float identifier : A9IIIII";</p>
<p>PLATFORM_NUMBER:_FillValue = " ";</p></td>
<td><p>WMO float identifier. WMO is the World Meteorological Organization. This platform number is unique.</p>
<p>Example: 6900045</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td><span id="dl3hidx36tx8" class="anchor"></span>PLATFORM_WIGOS_ID</td>
<td><p>char PLATFORM_WIGOS_ID(STRING17);</p>
<p>PLATFORM_WIGOS_ID:long_name = "Float unique identifier";</p>
<p>PLATFORM_WIGOS_ID:conventions = "WMO WIGOS float identifier: 0-22000-0-A9IIIII";</p>
<p>PLATFORM_WIGOS_ID:_FillValue = " ";</p></td>
<td><p><strong><del>This is an optional variable.</del></strong></p>
<p>WMO WIGOS float identifier. WMO is the World Meteorological Organization.</p>
<p>This platform number is unique within all observation platforms. For Argo floats, it is composed of "0-22000-0-", the Argo float prefix, followed by the WMO ID.</p>
<p>For example, for float 6900045:</p>
<p>PLATFORM_WIGOS_ID = "0-22000-0-6900045"</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>PTT</td>
<td><p>char PTT(STRING256);</p>
<p>PTT:long_name = "Transmission identifier (ARGOS, ORBCOMM, etc.)";</p>
<p>PTT:_FillValue = " ";</p></td>
<td><p>Transmission identifier of the float. Comma separated list for multi-beacon transmission.</p>
<p>Examples:</p>
<p>"22507" (example when the float is equipped with one ARGOS beacon)</p>
<p>"22598, 22768" (example when the float is equipped with 2 ARGOS beacons)</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>TRANS_SYSTEM</td>
<td><p>char TRANS_SYSTEM(N_TRANS_SYSTEM, STRING16);</p>
<p>TRANS_SYSTEM:long_name = "Telecommunication system used";</p>
<p>TRANS_SYSTEM:_FillValue = " ";</p></td>
<td><p>Name of the telecommunication system from reference table 10 (<a href="https://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/R10/"><u>https://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/R10/</u></a>).</p>
<p>Example: "ARGOS"</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>TRANS_SYSTEM_ID</td>
<td><p>char TRANS_SYSTEM_ID(N_TRANS_SYSTEM, STRING32);</p>
<p>TRANS_SYSTEM_ID:long_name = "Program identifier used by the transmission system";</p>
<p>TRANS_SYSTEM_ID:_FillValue = " ";</p></td>
<td><p>Program identifier of the telecommunication subscription. DACs can use N/A or alternative of their choice when not applicable (e.g. : Iridium or Orbcomm)</p>
<p>Example: 38511 is a program number for all the beacons of an ARGOS customer.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>TRANS_FREQUENCY</td>
<td><p>char TRANS_FREQUENCY(N_TRANS_SYSTEM, STRING16);</p>
<p>TRANS_FREQUENCY:long_name = "Frequency of transmission from the float";</p>
<p>TRANS_FREQUENCY:units = "hertz";</p>
<p>TRANS_FREQUENCY:_FillValue = " ";</p></td>
<td><p>Frequency of transmission from the float.</p>
<p>Example: "1/44"</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>POSITIONING_SYSTEM</td>
<td><p>char POSITIONING_SYSTEM(N_POSITIONING_SYSTEM, STRING8);</p>
<p>POSITIONING_SYSTEM:long_name = "Positioning system";</p>
<p>POSITIONING_SYSTEM:_FillValue = " ";</p></td>
<td><p>Position system from reference table 9 (<a href="https://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/R09/"><u>https://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/R09/</u></a>). ARGOS or GPS are 2 positioning systems.</p>
<p>Example: "ARGOS"</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>PLATFORM_FAMILY</td>
<td><p>char PLATFORM_FAMILY(STRING256);</p>
<p>PLATFORM_FAMILY:long_name = "Category of instrument";</p>
<p>PLATFORM_FAMILY:conventions = "Argo reference table 22";</p>
<p>PLATFORM_FAMILY:_FillValue = " ";</p></td>
<td><p>Category of instrument.</p>
<p>See Argo reference table 22 (<a href="https://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/R22/"><u>https://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/R22/</u></a>).</p>
<p>Example: "FLOAT"</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>PLATFORM_TYPE</td>
<td><p>char PLATFORM_TYPE(STRING32);</p>
<p>PLATFORM_TYPE:long_name = "Type of float";</p>
<p>PLATFORM_TYPE:conventions = "Argo reference table 23";</p>
<p>PLATFORM_TYPE:_FillValue = " ";</p></td>
<td><p>Type of float.</p>
<p>See Argo reference table 23 (<a href="https://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/R23/"><u>https://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/R23/</u></a>).</p>
<p>Example: "APEX"</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>PLATFORM_MAKER</td>
<td><p>char PLATFORM_MAKER(STRING256);</p>
<p>PLATFORM_MAKER:long_name = "Name of the manufacturer";</p>
<p>PLATFORM_MAKER:conventions = "Argo reference table 24";</p>
<p>PLATFORM_MAKER:_FillValue = " ";</p></td>
<td><p>Name of the manufacturer.</p>
<p>See Argo reference table 24 (<a href="https://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/R24/"><u>https://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/R24/</u></a>).</p>
<p>Example: "TWR"</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>FLOAT_FIRMWARE_VERSION</td>
<td><p>char FLOAT_FIRMWARE_VERSION(STRING64);</p>
<p>FLOAT_FIRMWARE_VERSION:long_name = "Firmware version for the float";</p>
<p>FLOAT_FIRMWARE_VERSION:_FillValue = " ";</p></td>
<td><p>The float firmware version. This is specified as per the format on the manufacturer’s manual.</p>
<p>char FLOAT_FIRMWARE_VERSION(<strong>STRING32</strong>) is also accepted.</p>
<p>Example: "072804"</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>FLOAT_MANUAL_VERSION</td>
<td><p>char FLOAT_MANUAL_VERSION(STRING16);</p>
<p>FLOAT_MANUAL_VERSION:long_name = "Manual version for the float";</p>
<p>FLOAT_MANUAL_VERSION:_FillValue = " ";</p></td>
<td><p>The version date or number for the manual for each float.</p>
<p>char FLOAT_MANUAL_VERSION(<strong>STRING128</strong>) is also accepted.</p>
<p>Example: "110610", "004"</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>FLOAT_SERIAL_NO</td>
<td><p>char FLOAT_SERIAL_NO(STRING32);</p>
<p>FLOAT_SERIAL_NO:long_name = "Serial number of the float";</p>
<p>FLOAT_SERIAL_NO:_FillValue = " ";</p></td>
<td><p>This field should contain only the serial number of the float.</p>
<p>Example: "1679"</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>STANDARD_FORMAT_ID</td>
<td><p>char STANDARD_FORMAT_ID(STRING16);</p>
<p>STANDARD_FORMAT_ID:long_name = "Standard format number to describe the data format type for each float";</p>
<p>STANDARD_FORMAT_ID:_FillValue = " ";</p></td>
<td><p>Standardized format number as described in the online reference table: <a href="https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/16iTji2i9tLh2PfiiMItfhaQybQB1NLAhj4s0mDML5yY/edit#gid=9"><u>https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/16iTji2i9tLh2PfiiMItfhaQybQB1NLAhj4s0mDML5yY/edit#gid=9</u></a></p>
<p>This table cross references to individual DAC format numbers.</p>
<p>Example: "1010151"</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DAC_FORMAT_ID</td>
<td><p>char DAC_FORMAT_ID(STRING16);</p>
<p>DAC_FORMAT_ID:long_name = "Format number used by the DAC to describe the data format type for each float";</p>
<p>DAC_FORMAT_ID:_FillValue = " ";</p></td>
<td><p>Format numbers used by individual DACs to describe each float type.</p>
<p>This is cross-referenced to a standard format id as outlined in the online reference table: <a href="https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/16iTji2i9tLh2PfiiMItfhaQybQB1NLAhj4s0mDML5yY/edit#gid=9"><u>https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/16iTji2i9tLh2PfiiMItfhaQybQB1NLAhj4s0mDML5yY/edit#gid=9</u></a></p>
<p>Example: "A9"</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>WMO_INST_TYPE</td>
<td><p>char WMO_INST_TYPE(STRING4);</p>
<p>WMO_INST_TYPE:long_name = "Coded instrument type";</p>
<p>WMO_INST_TYPE:conventions = "Argo reference table 8";</p>
<p>WMO_INST_TYPE:_FillValue = " ";</p></td>
<td><p>Instrument type from WMO code table 1770. A subset of WMO table 1770 is documented in the reference table 8 (<a href="https://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/R08/"><u>https://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/R08/</u></a>).</p>
<p>Example: "846" (corresponding to Webb Research float, Seabird sensor)</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>PROJECT_NAME</td>
<td><p>char PROJECT_NAME(STRING64);</p>
<p>PROJECT_NAME:long_name = "Name of the project";</p>
<p>PROJECT_NAME:_FillValue = " ";</p></td>
<td>Name of the project that operates the float. Multiple projects are separated by commas.<br />
Example: "GYROSCOPE, GMMC"</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>PROGRAM_NAME</td>
<td><p>char PROGRAM_NAME(STRING64);</p>
<p>PROGRAM_NAME:long_name = "Name of the program";</p>
<p>PROGRAM_NAME:_FillValue = " ";</p></td>
<td><p>This variable becomes mandatory in meta version 3.2.</p>
<p>The overarching program(s) of which the float is a part. A program consists of a set of related and possibly interdependent projects (PROJECT_NAME) that meet an overarching objective. A program defines a group of floats managed by the same lead agency. It materializes the implementing, operating, and responsible team.</p>
<p>The PROGRAM_NAME list is managed by OceanOPS. Detailed definition of PROGRAM_NAME is available here: <a href="https://www.ocean-ops.org/metadata/#concept-definitions"><u>https://www.ocean-ops.org/metadata/#concept-definitions</u></a>.</p>
<p>See Argo reference table 41 (<a href="https://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/R41/"><u>https://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/R41/</u></a>).</p>
<p>Examples: "Argo INDIA" or "Argo UK Bio" or "Argo UW"</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>DATA_CENTRE</td>
<td><p>char DATA_CENTRE(STRING2);</p>
<p>DATA_CENTRE:long_name = "Data centre in charge of float real-time processing";</p>
<p>DATA_CENTRE:conventions = "Argo reference table 4";</p>
<p>DATA_CENTRE:_FillValue = " ";</p></td>
<td><p>Code of the data centre in charge of the float data management. The data centre codes are described in the reference table 4 (<a href="https://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/R04/"><u>https://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/R04/</u></a>).</p>
<p>Example: "ME" (for MEDS)</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>PI_NAME</td>
<td><p>char PI_NAME (STRING64);</p>
<p>PI_NAME:long_name = "Name of the principal investigator";</p>
<p>PI_NAME:_FillValue = " ";</p></td>
<td><p>Name of the principal investigator responsible for the profiling float. Valid PI names are listed in reference table 40 (<a href="https://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/R40/"><u>https://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/R40/</u></a>). The generic convention to follow is "Firstname1 [Firstname2] LASTNAME". Multiple names can be concatenated, separated by commas.</p>
<p>Example: "Julia UITZ, Birgit KLEIN"</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>ANOMALY</td>
<td><p>char ANOMALY(STRING256);</p>
<p>ANOMALY:long_name = "Describe any anomalies or problems the float may have had";</p>
<p>ANOMALY:_FillValue = " ";</p></td>
<td><p>This field describes any anomaly or problem the float may have had.</p>
<p>This field is also used to record ending causes (see <a href="#reference-table-31-ending_cause"><u>§3.29</u></a>).</p>
<p>Example: "the immersion drift is not stable."</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>BATTERY_TYPE</td>
<td><p>char BATTERY_TYPE(STRING64);</p>
<p>BATTERY_TYPE:long_name = "Type of battery packs in the float";</p>
<p>BATTERY_TYPE:_FillValue = " ";</p></td>
<td><p>Describes the type of battery packs in the float.</p>
<p>BATTERY_TYPE syntax uses both reference table 33 altLabel (<a href="https://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/R33/"><u>https://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/R33/</u></a>) and reference table 34 altLabel (<a href="https://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/R34/"><u>https://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/R34/</u></a>) with the following convention: &lt;R33-battery_maker&gt; &lt;R34-battery_type&gt; &lt;voltage&gt; V [+&lt;R33-battery_maker&gt; &lt;R34-battery_type&gt; &lt;voltage&gt; V].</p>
<p>&lt;voltage&gt; stands for the initial battery voltage.</p>
<p>Examples:</p>
<p>"<em>ELECTROCHEM Lithium 15.0 V</em>"</p>
<p>"<em>TADIRAN Lithium 15 V</em> + <em>TADIRAN Lithium 12.1 V"</em></p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>BATTERY_PACKS</td>
<td><p>char BATTERY_PACKS(STRING64);</p>
<p>BATTERY_PACKS:long_name = "Configuration of battery packs in the float";</p>

## Configuration parameters 
This section describes the configuration parameters for a float. It is important to note that configuration parameters are float settings selected by the PI, not measurements reported by the float.

Configuration parameters may or may not be reported by a float.

Configuration parameter names are identified by the "CONFIG" prefix.

For each configuration parameter, the name and the value of the parameter are recorded.

All parameter names are standardized and are available in the online reference table 18 ([<u>https://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/R18/</u>](https://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/R18/)).

The configuration table 18 contains both Core Argo configuration parameters (Identifier starting with CC\*, or AltLabel starting with "Core Config") and BGC-Argo sensor configuration parameters (Identifier starting with CB\*, or AltLabel starting with "BGC Config"). If you are a new user or have only standard Argo floats you should first check the Core Argo configuration parameters list which has the basic set of configuration parameters that caters for most of the standard float types. If your float carries additional BGC-Argo sensors you will also need to refer to the BGC-Argo sensor configuration parameters list. To request for new configuration parameter names, please either send an e-mail to the table responsible(s), who are mentioned in the [<u>readme of ArgoVocab Github</u>](https://github.com/OneArgo/ArgoVocabs?tab=readme-ov-file#VI-Management-special-case-for-R03-R14-and-R18-tables), or open a new AVFTT ticket ([<u>https://github.com/OneArgo/ArgoVocabs/issues</u>](https://github.com/OneArgo/ArgoVocabs/issues)).

The mission settings or parameter values are recorded as numbers (the NetCDF field type is float). In this scheme, strings will need to be converted to numbers and will require numeric codes for the relevant parameters. How to translate back these numeric codes to a string value is detailed in the definition field of [<u>https://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/R18/</u>](https://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/R18/). Only a few existing parameters are concerned. If new floats with new configuration parameters (as strings) are introduced, then equivalent numeric codes must also be added to the table by the proposer of the new configuration parameter.

The mission is used to record information that changes from cycle to cycle, for instance when a float changes its mission from 3 shallow profiles to 1 deep profile. The shallow and deep profiles will have different mission numbers. The value of the mission number is recorded in CONFIG_MISSION_NUMBER.

Configuration parameters are separated into two types.

1\) Pre-deployment or launch configuration parameters that are the ‘configured’ start settings of the float and the initial mission configuration parameters for the first cycle. These parameters with the dimension N_LAUNCH_CONFIG_PARAM, are stored in LAUNCH_CONFIG_PARAMETER_NAME and LAUNCH_CONFIG_PARAMETER_VALUE.

2\) After deployment,configuration parameters define float behavior for each mission, including all applicable mandatory and highly-desirable parameters and any other parameters that change during the life of the float are reported as mission settings. These parameters with the dimension N_CONFIG_PARAM, need to be reported in the CONFIG_PARAMETER_NAME and CONFIG_PARAMETER_VALUE variables. The mission parameters for the first cycle must also be reported in the launch section.

The parameter CONFIG_MISSION_COMMENT can be used to store information about the mission or whether the mission was set pre-deployment or transmitted by the float (free form field).

### Note on floats with multiple missions
Typically, an Argo float configuration is valid for the whole life of the float. Each cycle is repeated with the same behavior (one configuration).

However, some floats may be configured to change their behavior from cycle to cycle (multiple configurations).

When there is only one configuration, CONFIG_MISSION_NUMBER is set to 1: all the cycles are programmed to be the same. Note that in this case; floats will still have a set of pre-deployment/launch configuration information that contains all the start settings for the float. So for a float with one basic mission, it will have launch configuration parameters and mission 1 configuration parameters (typically just the mission critical subset).

When there are multiple configurations, the configuration from the first cycle has CONFIG_MISSION_NUMBER set to 1. Each subsequent configuration change will be recorded as additional entries in CONFIG_MISSION_NUMBER, with the value increased sequentially by the integer one. All variables from mission 1 must be repeated in subsequent missions. Floats with multiple configurations still record pre-deployment or launch information in: LAUNCH_CONFIG_PARAMETER_NAME and LAUNCH_CONFIG_PARAMETER_VALUE.

Argo best practice, and our recommendation to users, is a minimum of configuration missions. If there is a change to one or more of the configuration parameters that does not repeat a previous configuration then a new mission number must be used. If the configuration parameters change, but mirror a previous mission then that mission number should be re-used. In extremely complex cases where mission changes are unclear, then a new mission number can be used for each cycle. Users should be aware that the metafile will need to be rewritten each time a new mission number is added.

Some floats conduct a pressure-activated test mission after deployment (i.e. some SOLO floats) where they essentially ‘wake-up’ at depth and return to the surface. This is not a normal mission in any way, and the floats do not use their configuration parameters in this first ‘test’ cycle. In this case you would assign a fill value to CONFIG_MISSION_NUMBER.

### Determining which mission applies to a particular float cycle
Users are able to determine which mission applies to each cycle by looking at the CONFIG_MISSION_NUMBER(N_CYCLE) variable in the trajectory files, and the CONFIG_MISSION_NUMBER(N_PROF) variable in the profile files.  
See section "[<u>§2.2.4</u>](#general-information-for-each-profile) General information for each profile" and "[<u>§2.3.6</u>](#n_cycle-dimension-variable-group) N_CYCLE dimension variable group").

**Example**

<img src="images/image4.jpg" style="width:6.29167in;height:3.3125in" />In the above example, there are 3 different float behaviors to record, (with park depth varying between 1500, 2000 and 1700 db). Each of these new behaviors requires a new mission number. This is in addition to the pre-deployment or launch information:

> CONFIG_PARAMETER_NAME = "CONFIG_ParkPressure_dbar"  
> CONFIG_PARAMETER_VALUE = "1500"  
> CONFIG_MISSION_NUMBER = 1

> CONFIG_MISSION_NUMBER = 3
>
> A further example for a float with multiple missions and changes to multiple configuration parameters is shown below.

In this example there are 11 pre-deployment/launch configuration parameters for this float which are set before launch. Of this set, the last four are mission critical parameters that change and control float behavior; these are reported in subsequent missions (missions 1 to n). For this float, the depth, at which the float parks, changes in missions 2 and 3 (with changes in two configuration parameters). For mission 4, the park depth stays the same as for mission 3 but now the park sampling period has changed. For mission 5, the park sampling period changes again. All configuration parameters from mission 1 must still be reported for each subsequent mission, even those that do not change.

## Float sensor and parameter information 
A **sensor** is a device used to measure a physical parameter. Sensor outputs are provided in parameter counts and need to be converted into parameter physical units using a calibration equation. This conversion can be done onboard the float or during the decoding process.

A **parameter** is a measurement of a physical phenomenon; it can be provided by a sensor (in sensor counts or in physical units) or computed (derived) from other parameters.

A sensor can measure 1 to N parameter(s). A parameter can be measured by 1 or N sensor(s).

### Float sensor information 
This section contains information about the sensors of the profiler.

A list of standardized Argo sensor names is given in reference table 25 ([<u>https://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/R25/</u>](https://vocab.nerc.ac.uk/collection/R25/)).

Each ocean state parameter recorded in an Argo profile or trajectory file must be considered its own sensor in this context. This is necessary to record the sensor serial numbers, etc. Thus a CTD which records PRES, TEMP, and PSAL should be considered 3 separate sensors (CTD_PRES, CTD_TEMP, CTD_CNDC respectively), as all 3 parameters are reported in the Argo profile and trajectory files. In comparison, an OPTODE only has DOXY reported in Argo NetCDF files, thus it should be considered a single sensor (OXYGEN_OPTODE or OXYGEN_ELECTROCHEMICAL) even though the sensor also reports TEMP_DOXY. All intermediate variables that do not appear in the core Argo files, even though they may appear in the 'raw' form (i.e. in the BGC-Argo B-file), do not have to be listed as a separate sensor. This is especially true if there is not a unique serial number for the sensor.

## Float predeployment calibration information 
This section contains information about the calibration of the profiler. The calibration described in this section is an instrumental calibration, performed mainly by the sensor manufacturer. The delayed mode calibration, performed by a data analysis, is described in the profile file (see Section [<u>§2.2.6</u>](#scientific-calibration-information-for-each-profile)).

The PREDEPLOYMENT_CALIB\_\* parameters in the table below link to the PARAMETER variable listed in [<u>§2.4.7.2</u>](#float-parameter-information). It is critical that these are ordered in the same way so that calibration information is assigned to the correct parameter.

### PREDEPLOYMENT_CALIB \_EQUATION SYNTAX GUIDELINES
1.  Calculation symbols used in PREDEPLOYMENT_CALIB_EQUATION

|                     |                                                                          |
|---------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Symbol**          | **Meaning**                                                              |
| =                   | Equal                                                                    |
| \- , + , / , \*     | Minus, plus, divide, multiply                                            |
| log , log10, exp    | Natural logarithm, Base-10 logarithm, exponential (power of e)           |
| ^                   | Power function                                                           |
| SUM                 | Sum                                                                      |
| ( )                 | Indicators of grouping or enclosing or delimiters of index               |
| .                   | Decimal separator                                                        |
| \>= , \<= , \> , \< | Greater than or equal to, less than or equal to, greater than, less than |

2.  Punctuation used in PREDEPLOYMENT_CALIB_EQUATION

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 20%" />
<col style="width: 79%" />
</colgroup>
<tbody>
<tr class="odd">
<td><strong>Symbol</strong></td>
<td><strong>Meaning</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td><blockquote>
<p>,</p>
</blockquote></td>
<td>Separates out extra information in a sentence</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td><blockquote>
<p>;</p>
</blockquote></td>
<td>Separates different sets of equation</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td><blockquote>
<p>:</p>
</blockquote></td>
<td>Before an equation that follows an explanation sentence</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td><blockquote>
<p>.</p>
</blockquote></td>
<td>Marks the end of the sentence</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

3.  Order of presentation

The equation is presented in the following order:

- Elementary pieces of calculation are first presented

- Then intermediary equations

- Then the final equation

The final equation can be completed by comments to give some guidance.

Example from the “Processing BGC-Argo nitrate

concentration at the DAC Level” document ([<u>https://dx.doi.org/10.13155/46121</u>](https://dx.doi.org/10.13155/46121)) :

“NITRATE= MOLAR_NITRATE/rho\*1000, where rho is the potential density \[kg/m^3\] calculated from the CTD data.”

<td><blockquote>
<p>.</p>
</blockquote></td>
<td><blockquote>
<p>Decimal separator</p>
</blockquote></td>

<tr class="even">
<td><blockquote>

2.  Notes on reporting PREDEPLOYMENT_CALIB_COEFFICIENT

For reporting PREDEPLOYMENT_CALIB_COEFFICIENT

- The exact name used in PREDEPLOYMENT_CALIB_EQUATION (including spelling and lower or upper case) should be reported in the key-value pairs

- If possible, the key-value pairs should be presented in the same order as they appear in PREDEPLOYMENT_CALIB_EQUATION (n.b.: a possible exception to this recommendation could relate to, e.g., grouping the spectrum values to ease readability)

Parsing order:

*1.* *”;”*

*2.* *“,”*

*3.* *“=”*
